entities.summary: Charles Lewis Camp was an American palaeontologist and zoologist, working from the University of California, Berkeley. He took part in excavations at the 'Placerias Quarry', in 1930 and the forty Shonisaurus skeleton discoveries of the 1960s, in what is now the Berlin-Ichthyosaur State Park. Camp served as the third director of the University of California Museum of Paleontology from 1930 to 1949, and coincidentally as chair of the UC Berkeley Paleontology Department between 1939 and 1949. Camp named a number of species of marine reptiles such as Shonisaurus and Plotosaurus, as well as the dinosaur Segisaurus.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Camp's discoveries of Shonisaurus and Plotosaurus provided crucial insights into marine reptile evolution, while his leadership at the University of California Museum of Paleontology helped shape the field of paleontology in North America. His work laid the groundwork for future research and conservation efforts.
